fixes.answer: For many people, fashion is a genuine form of [[self-expression]], allowing them to communicate their personality, mood and identity without words. It can boost confidence and create a sense of belonging to a particular group. For some, it is also an art form and a source of creativity. While I personally value comfort over trends, I completely understand why fashion [[holds such significance]]; it is a powerful, [[visual language]] of identity.
fixes.why: 'visual' and 'identity' are plain; marked 'self-expression', 'holds such significance', 'visual language'

fixes.answer: In some ways, yes. The rise of social media has made appearance more visible and, arguably, more important, with influencers constantly showcasing new trends. [[Fast fashion]] has also made trendy clothing cheap and accessible, [[fuelling]] constant consumption. However, past eras had their own strong fashion cultures too. So perhaps it is not that people care more, but that fashion has become more fast-paced, [[disposable]] and publicly displayed than ever before.

The environmental impact is unfortunately severe, particularly from fast fashion. The industry is a major consumer of water and a significant source of pollution and carbon emissions. The culture of buying cheap, disposable clothing generates enormous [[textile waste]], much of which ends up in landfill. So while fashion brings joy and self-expression, its current [[unsustainable]] model [[exacts a heavy toll]] on the planet that urgently needs addressing.
fixes.why: 'disposable' repeated from Q2 and 'toll' part of an idiom; marked 'textile waste' and 'exacts a heavy toll'

fixes.answer: Fashion has a [[powerful hold]] on young people. It is closely tied to identity and social acceptance, so what they wear can strongly affect their confidence and sense of belonging. Trends spread rapidly through social media, creating pressure to keep up, which can be expensive and stressful. While fashion can be a positive outlet for creativity, this [[relentless]] pressure to conform can also [[breed insecurity]] and unhealthy comparison.
fixes.why: 'stressful' and 'comparison' are plain; marked 'powerful hold' and 'breed insecurity'

fixes.answer: I anticipate sustainability will become a [[driving force]]. As awareness of fast fashion's harm grows, I expect a shift towards more durable, ethical and recycled clothing, and a move away from [[throwaway culture]]. Technology may also personalise fashion, and digital or virtual clothing could even emerge. So I am hopeful the future of fashion will be more sustainable, more conscious, and perhaps less [[wasteful]] than the current model.
fixes.why: 'sustainable' and 'conscious' are plain; marked 'driving force' and 'throwaway culture'

fixes.answer: Several changes are needed. On the industry side, brands should adopt ethical, eco-friendly production and be more transparent. Consumers can play a huge role by buying less, choosing quality over quantity, and embracing [[second-hand]] or recycled clothing. Repairing and reusing garments rather than discarding them also helps. Ultimately, moving away from a throwaway mindset towards more [[durable]], [[considered consumption]] is the most impactful solution.
fixes.why: 'throwaway' repeated and 'impactful' plain; marked 'second-hand' and 'considered consumption'

fixes.answer: Following trends can be fun and allows people to feel current, confident and part of a community. It is a [[creative outlet]] and can help people fit in socially. The disadvantages, though, are that constantly chasing trends is expensive, contributes to environmental waste, and can suppress genuine individuality. It can also foster insecurity. So while there is joy in it, an [[obsessive]] pursuit of trends can become both costly and [[superficial]].

I only partly agree. Excessive spending on constantly changing trends, particularly disposable fast fashion, can certainly be wasteful and financially [[imprudent]]. However, I would not dismiss fashion entirely, as it is a [[legitimate]] form of self-expression and creativity that brings people genuine joy and confidence. Investing in quality, lasting pieces is also sensible. So it is not inherently a waste; it becomes one only when pursued excessively and [[impulsively]].
